This file is the SOURCE now: the script compiles each `when` with new RegExp, and tests/guards/verify-changed-rules-resolve.test.ts asserts every `run` path exists. Data rather than code so the mapping is readable, diffable, and assertable from a CJS test — jest's node project cannot import an .mjs.
//noTestsNeeded: Paths that derive NO tests BY DESIGN, each with the reason. This is the
third category, and it exists because the empty-population refusal would
otherwise block a README edit: 'no rule covers this' and 'no test could
cover this' are different answers and only one of them is a problem.
Shrink-only in spirit — an entry here is a claim that nothing in the
sixteen test roots can observe a change to that path.

noTestsNeeded.why: Top-level prose for humans, and MEASURED rather than assumed: no test reads SECURITY.md or CHANGELOG.md from disk. README.md was in here on the same claim and is READ by b8-landing-no-passwords-grc (`const README = read('README.md')`), which checks the landing copy carries no credentials — so editing it derived NOTHING and read as a pass, which is the failure #2018 exists to prevent, inside these rules. It has its own path rule now. CLAUDE.md was already the acknowledged exception.

Tooling config with no test surface, and the three that remain are measured: no test reads .gitignore, .gitattributes or .editorconfig from disk. `.nvmrc` and `.npmrc` were in here on the same claim and both ARE read — deterministic-install reads .nvmrc, engine-strict-is-ci-only reads .npmrc — so they have a path rule now. `generated-artifacts-have-no-merge-driver` asserts .gitattributes has no merge driver, and that guard is reached by the content rule on the driver syntax itself, not by a path rule.
Editor-local settings; nothing in the repo reads them.

Top-level prose, measured rather than assumed: no test reads either from disk. Kept apart from the CONTRIBUTING/SECURITY/CHANGELOG entry so that one stays a statement about the files it names — README.md was removed from it after turning out to be read, and a wider regex is how that happens again. #2566.

Tooling with no test surface, measured: no test reads any of the three from disk. `next-env.d.ts` is generated by Next and listed first in tsconfig's `include`, but nothing asserts on its contents; `eslint.json` is a report artifact, not the config — `eslint.config.mjs` is the config and has a path rule. #2566.

Build artifacts tracked at the root by accident — #2567 proposes removing them and adding the matching .gitignore patterns. Declared here so the empty-population refusal does not block an unrelated PR that happens to touch one; this is a PARKING SPACE, not an endorsement. If #2567 lands, delete this entry in the same diff: the no-stale-entries test will demand it.

pathRules.why: A change under tests/ puts META-guards in scope — ones that grade the SHAPE of test code (hand-rolled file walks, comment strippers, guard-file ceilings) rather than the code under test. Measured twice: `file-collection-is-not-silently-empty` fired on a helper inside a new test, and its subject ("which guards exist") has nothing to do with any change topic.
Route coverage, the route inventory and the OpenAPI completeness contracts all range over the route tree, and none of them live beside the route.
The i18n gate checks bg/en key parity, orphans, drift and untranslated values across the whole catalogue, so one added key is a whole-catalogue question.
The generated spec is committed, so a path edit without `npm run openapi:generate` leaves it stale, and the contract snapshots pin its prose.
Schema-folder coverage, destructive-migration inverses and RLS guards are all derived from the schema rather than from the migration you wrote.

docs/ is NOT test-free, which is what I assumed when I first declared it so. Derived: 64 distinct docs files are read by tests, and the sweeps make it worse than a list suggests — no-legacy-brand scans docs for the previous brand name, so ANY file here can fail a guard, and vm-runbook-commands asserts every repo path docs/runbooks/production-vm.md names still exists. Even docs/implementation-notes/ is read by five guards. Found by editing the runbook and watching verify:changed report `none with a test surface` for a file its own guardrail reads.

Six guards read infra/: oi-3-alerting and oi-3-runbook-and-slos assert the declared alert policies and SLO targets, infra-directories-are-referenced fails when a directory here is referenced by nothing, and the restore-drill pair (shell-heredoc-no-live-backticks, restore-drill-remote-script) pins the quoted heredoc whose un-quoting left the drill dead for a month.

public/ is not static assets only. public/sw.js is the outbox's PARALLEL reimplementation — it cannot import from src/, so its copy is mirrored BY HAND and outbox-completion-mirrors-the-sw exists to enforce that mirror; eight test files across three roots read it (also sw-revision-stamp, sw-offline-route-integrity, web-push, the two registrar suites). public/fonts is pinned by vendored-font-integrity and font-preload-derived-from-lock. Before this rule a change to the service worker derived NOTHING.

Covers dependabot.yml too (dependabot-typescript-eslint-group and typescript-eslint-family-is-coherent both read it), not just workflows and scripts. Several guards assert against .github itself rather than against src: ci-failure-watchlist DERIVES the notifier's watch list from the workflow files, ci-aggregate-upstream-failure lifts each aggregate's run: block out of ci.yml and executes it, shell-heredoc-no-live-backticks pins the restore drill's quoted delimiter, and restore-drill-remote-script compares the payload byte-for-byte. Added because a 2026-10-25 change to three .github files derived ZERO paths and so ran the entire suite: the watchlist guard had to be run by hand to discover it was demanding the new workflow.

Compose/image guards assert drift against the repo-canonical files and the env template. tests/unit/deploy holds the EXECUTING tests for the deploy scripts — compare-running-state.py's exit codes, prune-backups.sh, verify-image-deps.mjs — which a structural guard cannot cover, since what matters there is what the script DOES. Those three suites sat outside this rule: #2288 created that root and did not add the line, so a change to the comparator never ran the suite written for it.
Dependency ratchets and the lockfile guards. A lockfile written by the wrong npm also drops platform `libc` constraints, which only a guard notices.
Rendered tests, the design-system drift guardrail and the public-surface guards all range over components rather than over the file you edited.
The default population for source changes. Broad on purpose: it is the root that held the failing assertion in the first of the three wrong subsets this issue records.
Several guards quote CLAUDE.md or assert that a claim in it is true, so editing it can fail a test with no code change at all.

These files are reached by jest.config.js rather than by `import`, so an import-derived blast radius scores every one of them at ZERO while they are the widest in the repo: globalSetup, globalTeardown, the `default` reporter's sibling, the `^@/env$` moduleNameMapper in BOTH projects, and the node project's two setupFilesAfterEnv entries. `tests` rather than a root list because the reach genuinely IS the whole run — and these six files change rarely, so the cost is paid almost never. #2531.

The shared-helper directory, and the measured reach is wide: blank-non-code.ts 266 importing suites across 5 roots, make-context.ts 212 (128 unit + 83 integration), db.ts 200, collect-files.ts 154, catalogue.ts 87. The `^tests/` rule selects only the META-guard roots, so editing the helper CLAUDE.md names as the canonical way to build a RequestContext ran NONE of its 211 importers. The list is the union over the DIRECTORY, so a two-importer helper pays for its neighbours — accepted deliberately, because the alternative is a rule per file and 27 rules go stale one at a time. Held true by tests/guards/verify-changed-covers-shared-test-helpers.test.ts, which re-derives the importers.

db-helper.ts has 197 importers, 193 of them in tests/integration, and db-probe.ts 198 — every integration suite reaches one or both. This is the miss that filed #2531: #2545 rewrote two steps of db-helper.ts into a `refuse(): never` and the derived population contained zero integration suites.

viewport.ts is imported by 30 suites, and setup.ts plus five component mocks are wired into the jsdom project by jest.config.js — setup.ts is the file CLAUDE.md names as the reason every rendered test runs as a PHONE, so changing its matchMedia stub changes which branch 271 suites execute.

The small tail of the same class: acknowledged-breaking-changes.ts is read by a contracts suite, __bearer-parity-helpers.ts by a unit suite, and tests/e2e/detail-paint-state.ts by a unit suite rather than by a spec. tests/e2e is deliberately NOT a run target here and must never become one — all 65 files there are `*.spec.ts` and jest's node project matches `*.test.ts` only, so the entry would name a real directory, satisfy verify-changed-rules-resolve, and contribute zero tests.

The two files that decide how every suite runs — jest.config.js owns the projects, testMatch, moduleNameMapper and reporters, and jest.setup.js is the node project's setupFilesAfterEnv. `tests` rather than a root list because the distinction that matters here is between who READS a file and whose behaviour it DECIDES: 6 tests name jest.config.js and 8 name jest.setup.js, while both decide the behaviour of all ~2,300. Same argument #2551 used for tests/setup and tests/mocks, and these change rarely so the cost is paid almost never. Before this, editing either derived NOTHING and `verify:changed` refused — correctly, since an empty population is a bare `jest` that sweeps the whole tree while printing `0 jest path(s)`. #2566.

The coverage gate's five group floors. The tooling that reads them is EXECUTED rather than guarded — tests/unit/coverage-tooling/coverage-scripts.test.ts runs merge-coverage, diff-coverage and check-coverage-thresholds — and coverage-parity-proof-current pins the shard count and the jest/istanbul versions beside the proof run id. 6 tests name this file across all three roots. #2566.

Which files are in the tsc program at all. `jest-project-instrumentation-parity` derives each jest project's tsconfig from jest.config.js and requires the same target, because ts-jest DOWNLEVELS `?.` under ES2017 and istanbul instruments the EMIT — the same file got two coverage shapes and a 26-statement file merged to 50. CLAUDE.md also records `incremental: true` reporting 0 errors for a file with 12. Matches tsconfig.scripts.json too: `exclude: ["scripts"]` in the base is why 34 of 51 scripts are in no program, which #2537 measured. 12 tests name it. #2566.

Build and tooling config that guards assert against. Measured readers: tailwind.config.js 25, playwright.config.ts 10, next.config.js 2, eslint.config.mjs 1, lighthouserc.json 2, prisma.config.ts 2. playwright.config.ts deliberately does NOT select tests/e2e — all 65 files there are `*.spec.ts` and jest's node project matches `*.test.ts` only, so such an entry would satisfy verify-changed-rules-resolve (the directory exists) and contribute zero tests, which is the trap #2551 recorded. postcss and release are grouped in with no measured reader, which over-includes on purpose: one regex that cannot miss a sibling beats six that can. #2566.

Dotfiles that ARE read from disk, two of them having been declared test-free on the opposite claim: deterministic-install reads .nvmrc and engine-strict-is-ci-only reads .npmrc. `.secret-patterns` is the single source of truth for the pre-commit hook and the C.2 guardrail, so a pattern removed there silently widens what may be committed. #2566.

Env templates. The readers are a MIX of literal and derived, which is why a literal-reference screen under-counts them: deploy-env-parity names .env.production.example and .env.staging.example directly, while no-duplicate-declarations collects every tracked `.example` with collectTrackedFiles and names none of them. `.env.test.example` has no literal reader at all and is still in that derived population — and scripts/ensure-env-test.mjs copies it to .env.test, so a key missing there surfaces as a test-DB failure far from its cause. #2566.

Was declared test-free under `No guard reads them` and is READ: b8-landing-no-passwords-grc does `const README = read('README.md')` and asserts the landing copy carries no credentials. So editing it derived NOTHING and read as a pass — the failure #2018 exists to prevent, occurring inside these rules. #2566.

contentRules.why: A NEW refusal code needs a Bulgarian entry and a name in the OpenAPI spec. Both guards live far from the throwing file, and both fired on #2035 after everything else was green.
A new path that stores uploaded bytes joins two derived populations — the metadata strippers and the past-due upload gate. #2030: four paths had escaped the second one.
Changing how an uploaded FORMAT is treated puts every suite holding a fixture of that format in scope. On #2035 that was 47 suites, 35 outside the import-derived set.
The lint ceiling counts SUPPRESSED findings, so a new disable can redden CI with no new warning. Re-run the ceiling AFTER the last edit — a stale run is one of the three failures this issue records.
The capability ruling and its gate coverage are checked by a derived population, not by the file holding the gate.
